thesis: Michael Duda argues that marketing is not merely an expense but a strategic asset that, when backed by capital, creates enduring brands capable of generating superior returns over time. He defines a brand as the net result of what a company does and how people feel, noting that great brands often possess a soul, are polarizing, and allow companies to earn high returns on capital even when the underlying product is indistinguishable from competitors.
